summary:
Project SCIENCE EXPLORERS is an interactive web application that maps and narrates the hidden history of human-made artifacts and discarded equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars.
​To address the storytelling challenge, our web app transforms complex NASA mission records and planetary landing coordinates into an engaging, accessible visual experience. Users can explore interactive planetary maps, click on specific landing zones from Apollo lunar missions to Mars rover sites, and uncover the stories behind the scientific instruments, descent stages, and hardware that remain on these worlds today.
​This project is important because it preserves humanity’s off-world heritage and makes space exploration tangible for learners of all ages. By connecting real NASA archival data with interactive storytelling, we inspire curiosity about past space milestones while highlighting the need for responsible, sustainable exploration in the future.
details: *Project: Abandoned but Not Forgotten* Our project gives a second life to abandoned objects in space — defunct satellites, spent rocket stages, and forgotten missions that are still orbiting Earth but no longer tracked by the public. We built an interactive web platform that pulls open data from NASA, CelesTrak, and Space-Track to map abandoned objects in Low Earth Orbit. Users can search any defunct satellite by name, launch year, or country, see its current orbit in 3D, learn its original mission, why it was abandoned, and what risk it poses today as space debris. A "Memory Wall" lets users add stories, photos, and facts about forgotten missions, so they are not lost from history. We also added a Reuse Simulator — using simple orbital mechanics, it suggests what could be done with the object: de-orbit it safely, move it to a graveyard orbit, or repurpose its parts for future missions. *Benefits and Intended Impact 1. Awareness: Makes the invisible problem of space debris visible to students and the public. 2. Education: Turns 60+ years of forgotten space history into an interactive learning tool. 3. Sustainability: Encourages thinking about responsible space use and debris mitigation for future missions. Our goal is to make people care about what we leave behind in space, just like we care about what we leave behind on Earth. *Tools, Languages & Software Used* Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, http://Three.js for 3D orbit visualization Backend / Data: Python, NASA Open APIs, CelesTrak TLE data Design: Figma, Canva Hosting: GitHub Pages / Vercel *How is it creative?* Instead of just showing dots on a map, we treat each satellite like a person with a story — born, worked, abandoned, but not forgotten. The combination of real-time tracking + storytelling + reuse ideas makes a technical problem emotional and memorable. *Factors our team considered* Accuracy of orbital data, simplicity for non-technical users, low internet usage so it works in classrooms, and accessibility for mobile users.
